text:
amira: Hey team, stuck on quickstart. curl -> 200, SDK -> 402 PaymentRequired workspace_billing_missing. Console says billing is attached. Very confusing.

onboarding-bot: Welcome! Workspace 'acme-sandbox' created. Attach billing at https://console.redwood.ai/billing to enable paid endpoints.

jas: Did you use the CLI to switch workspaces or pass a workspace id to the sample?

amira: I ran `redwood workspace list` and it showed two: `acme-org` (billed) and `acme-sandbox` (created by the quickstart). I thought the SDK would inherit the CLI selection. I ran `redwood workspace switch acme-org`.

cli-bot: Note: CLI workspace selection is stored in ~/.redwood/config and used by the CLI only. SDKs read env var REDWOOD_WORKSPACE or an explicit header `X-Redwood-Workspace`.

amira: aha. The sample's docker-compose.yml sets REDWOOD_WORKSPACE=acme-sandbox (leftover from CI sample). That workspace doesn't have billing. So the SDK made the call scoped to acme-sandbox and gateway returned 402.

leo: That explains curl working — your host curl used the user token and no workspace override, so the gateway billed against your default billed workspace. The containerized sample used the env var that pointed to an unpaid workspace.

amira: Logged into console, acme-sandbox is present but shows "billing required" even though org has a billing account. I assumed all workspaces under the org inherit billing.

jas: Clarification: billing can be org-level (applies to all workspaces) or workspace-level depending on your org settings. In this org the billing wasn't auto-attached to newly created workspaces. That's why acme-sandbox needed an explicit billing link.

amira: Thanks. Two UX things I hit: (1) quickstart created the sandbox workspace with no prompt and the sample repo had REDWOOD_WORKSPACE pointing to it, (2) SDK error message just said 402 PaymentRequired without telling me which workspace was billed or which workspace was used.

devex: Action items: (A) update quickstart to avoid baking a REDWOOD_WORKSPACE env into samples; prefer explicit startup log showing workspace id used, (B) make SDK error include workspace id/name when returning billing errors, (C) add a CLI hint after `workspace create` to remind users to attach billing or confirm billing inheritance.

leo: Small repro commands for docs: `docker-compose run sample_env echo $REDWOOD_WORKSPACE` and `redwood workspace show` to compare. Also check `REDWOOD_API_KEY` vs `REDWOOD_KEY` if things look off.

amira: Workaround: I unset REDWOOD_WORKSPACE in the container and re-ran — first call succeeded. Then I explicitly attached billing to acme-sandbox via console and re-set REDWOOD_WORKSPACE; still works.

jas: Filed RED-7002: "quickstart: don't inject REDWOOD_WORKSPACE by default; show chosen workspace in sample startup log; SDK to include workspace id in 402 messages."

devex: Also propose small CLI change: when user switches workspace, show a one-liner if that workspace lacks billing: `Warning: workspace acme-sandbox has no billing attached - calls to paid endpoints will return 402`. That would prevent this exact trap.

amira: That would have saved me 20 minutes. PRs: I'll open a tiny change to the sample repo to remove the hardcoded REDWOOD_WORKSPACE and add a startup message.

docs: I'll add a troubleshooting entry: "402 on first SDK call" with checklist: verify REDWOOD_API_KEY, ensure REDWOOD_WORKSPACE not pointing to unpaid workspace, and how to check workspace billing in console.

amira: First successful call after unsetting REDWOOD_WORKSPACE! :tada: Leaving thread for onboarding playbook.

leo: Nice. We'll follow up on RED-7002 and CLI hint. Thanks for reporting.
